purview of respective State/UT Governments. However, under NAM, there is a provision of
financial assistance for the establishment of new Ayush colleges in the States where availability
of Ayush teaching institutions is inadequate in Government Sector and accordingly State/UT
Governments may avail the eligible financial assistance by submitting the suitable proposals
through SAAPs as per the provision of NAM guidelines. As per the proposals received from
State/UT Governments, 13 new Ayush education institutes have been supported for
establishment as per the provision of NAM guideline from 2014-15 to 2022-23 in different

modern and traditional healthcare systems;
(c) whether the Government has any plan to push investments for further Research and
Development in AYUSH due to lack of their evidence based efficacy; and
(d) if so, the details thereof alongwith the steps taken/ proposed to be taken in this regard?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF AYUSH
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL)
(a) and (b) Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) on 16th February,
2013 notified Health Insurance Regulation 2013 with provisions inter alia for ‘AYUSH Coverage’
in Health Insurance policies under clause 5(I). IRDAI modified the Guidelines on
Standardization in Health Insurance Business vide circular No.
IRDA/HLT/REG/CIR/209/11/2019 dated 26/11/2019 by incorporating the definitions of
“AYUSH Hospital” and “AYUSH Day Care Centre”. As per the information received from
IRDAI, 29 insurance companies now provide products that cover AYUSH treatment.
(c) and (d) The Ministry of Ayush has made several initiatives to increase investment in the
AYUSH sector for further Research and Development, which are as follows;
i. The Ministry of Ayush has implemented the Central Sector Scheme namely
AYURGYANScheme having two components, i.e., (i) Capacity Building & Continuing
Medical Education (CME) in Aysuh (ii) Research & Innovation in AYUSH from the FY
2021-22. Under the research & Innovation in AYUSH, financial assistance is provided to
the Organizations/Institutions for research studies, for promotion of AYUSH research and
to support research & Innovation in AYUSH

ii. Ministry of Ayushhas implemented Central Sector Scheme, namely AYURSWASTHYA
Yojana and it has two components i.e. (i) AYUSH and Public Health (PHI) (ii) Centre of
Excellence (CoE). The AYURSWASTHYAYojana was implemented in the Financial
Year 2021-22 .The detailed guidelines of Ayurswasthya Yojana are available at:
https://main.ayush.gov.in/hi/schemes-2/central-sector-scheme/ayurswasthya-yojana/
iii. The Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) under Ministry of
Ayush, is an apex body for the formulation, coordination, development and promotion of
research on scientific lines in Ayurveda. CCRAS executes its research programmes with
a network of 30 peripheral Institutes/centres/units throughout India with the headquarters
at New Delhi, responsible for control, monitoring and supervision. Research work of
CCRAS is executed through Intra mural and collaborative studies in areas of Clinical
Research, Fundamental Research, Pharmacology Research, Medicinal Plant Research
(Medico-Ethno Botanical survey, Cultivation, Pharmacognosy) Drug standardization
Research and Literary Research & Documentation.
iv. Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine(CCRUM) under the Ministry of Ayush
is engaged in evidence based research under its clinical research programme. Clinical
validation studies are being carried out on the pharmacopoeial / classical drugs through
its 19 clinical research Institutes. The researchers are conducting research in Unani
medicine on different modern parameters and published in various peer reviewed
National/International Journals. Outcome of these researches are also presented in
seminar / conferences / workshops / training programme etc.
v. Central Council for Research in Siddha (CCRS) under the Ministry of Ayush mainly
focuses on clinical research including safety and efficacy studies of Siddha drugs,
validation of the fundamental principles, drug standardization and quality control, survey
and cultivation of medicinal plants and literary research. 54 books, 10 Patents and 650
scientific research articles have been published by CCRS. CCRS is equipped with state-
of-the-art infrastructure with sophisticated instruments and facilities The Council is
engaged in multifaceted research activities. In the area of clinical research, pre-clinical
Pharmacological / Toxicological studies, Open label trials, multi-centric Randomized
Controlled Trials (RCTs) are being conducted for acute and chronic diseases. The main
emphasis is on diseases of national health priority with a view to develop safe and
effective Siddha treatments.
vi. Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy (CCRH) under the Ministry of Ayush is
for scientific research in homoeopathy. It formulates, coordinates and promotes research
activities through its 27 institutes/units and 7 treatment centers across the country. CCRH
executes research programmes such as Clinical Research, Drug Proving, Drug
Verification, Drug Standardization, Fundamental Research, Epidemic research, either in
intramural mode or in collaboration with different institutes of repute and Public Health
programs such as SC/ST Health camps and growing of exotic/indigenous medicinal
plants used in Homoeopathy.
